description: Sayadieh Fish Rice with Caramelized Onion is a truly iconic Middle Eastern seafood dish, celebrated for its rich flavors and aromatic spices. Flaky white fish is perfectly cooked and served over fragrant rice, deeply infused with the sweet, savory essence of golden caramelized onions. This traditional meal offers a harmonious blend of textures and tastes, making it a beloved centerpiece for family gatherings.

instructions.title: Prepare the Fish
instructions.text: Season the fish fillets generously with 1 teaspoon of salt, 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper, and 1 tablespoon of the Sayadieh spice blend. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Pan-fry the fish for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Set aside.

instructions.title: Caramelize the Onions
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the remaining 1/4 cup of olive oil over medium heat. Add the thinly sliced onions and a pinch of salt. Cook slowly, stirring occasionally, for 20-25 minutes until the onions are deeply golden brown and caramelized. This is crucial for the dishs flavor.

instructions.title: Infuse the Rice Base
instructions.text: Remove about half of the caramelized onions and set them aside for garnish. To the remaining onions in the pot, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of Sayadieh spice blend, 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric powder, and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Stir and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Cook the Rice
instructions.text: Add the rinsed basmati rice to the pot with the spiced onions. Stir well to coat the rice grains. Pour in the fish broth or water and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.

instructions.title: Assemble and Rest
instructions.text: Once the rice is cooked, remove the pot from the heat and let it rest, covered, for 10 minutes. Gently fluff the rice with a fork.

instructions.title: Serve Sayadieh
instructions.text: To serve, spread the fluffy rice onto a large serving platter. Arrange the cooked fish fillets over the rice. Garnish generously with the reserved caramelized onions, toasted pine nuts, and fresh chopped parsley. Drizzle with fresh lemon juice before serving.

tips: For a deeper flavor, use fish stock made from the fish bones. If unavailable, vegetable broth or water can be used, but fish stock enhances the authentic taste.
The key to authentic Sayadieh is the dark caramelization of the onions. Do not rush this step; it develops the signature color and sweet, savory depth of the dish.
Serve Sayadieh immediately after assembly. A side of tahini sauce or a simple cucumber-tomato salad complements the richness of the dish beautifully.
